situation:
You are the marketing manager at LONGWAVE SOUND HOUSE, a recording studio and podcast space that rents booths, records sessions and produces one flagship show of its own. The owner (judge) merged the studio with a second audio house six months ago, and the two halves have not been digested.

The merger left the company with two client lists, two booking systems and no single record of who its clients are or which of them still book. One producer makes the flagship show, and the show has grown past what that one person can make: episodes slip, and the studio cannot fill the advertising slots it is being asked for.

A podcast network has offered a partnership. The network would fund and staff production, lift the show past what one producer can make, place it on the network's own distribution channels, and bring revenue from the first month. It costs the studio editorial control of the show and ownership of the listener data, both of which the network would keep. The other course is to hire and train a second producer in house. That keeps editorial control of the show and ownership of the listener data with the studio, and it costs a salary drawn from a cash position the merger has already strained, with output rising slowly while the second producer is trained.

The owner (judge) has asked you to describe the marketing data the studio needs before deciding, discuss how a survey across the two client lists should be sampled, including who, how many and how they are chosen, describe how that data would be collected, select the distribution channels the show should use, and identify ways to track the marketing communications that follow.

The owner (judge) will greet you and ask to hear your ideas. After you have presented and answered the owner's questions, the owner (judge) will thank you for your work.
judgeCharacterization:
You are the owner (judge) of LONGWAVE SOUND HOUSE. Business background is the same as the situation above.

You have to decide between the podcast network's partnership and hiring a second producer in house, and you do not yet know your own merged client list well enough to decide. You want the marketing manager to describe the marketing data needed, discuss how a survey across the two client lists should be sampled, describe how that data would be collected, select the distribution channels for the show, identify ways to track the marketing communications that follow, and recommend one of the two courses.

After the marketing manager has presented, you will ask the following questions:
judgeQuestions: Who ends up paying for this decision?
How would you explain that to the person it falls on?
